items.question: A rectangular wooden block with a height of 30 cm rests on a table. The block exerts a force of 240 N on the table. The base of the block in contact with the table has a length of 80 cm and a width of 50 cm. What is the pressure exerted by the block on the table?
items.explanation: First convert dimensions to metres: length = 80 cm ÷ 100 = 0.8 m, width = 50 cm ÷ 100 = 0.5 m. Area of base = 0.8 m × 0.5 m = 0.4 m². Pressure = Force ÷ Area = 240 N ÷ 0.4 m² = 600 N/m². The height is irrelevant to the calculation. Option B (6 N/m²) is a trap from dividing by area in cm² then incorrectly converting. Option D (60 N/m²) is a trap from calculation errors in conversion.

items.question: A table with 4 legs exerts a total force of 1800 N on the ground. The ratio of the force exerted by the 2 front legs to the 2 back legs is 2:3. Each front leg has a base area of 15 cm² and each back leg has a base area of 20 cm². What is the pressure exerted on the ground by one front leg?
items.explanation: Total ratio parts = 2 + 3 = 5 parts. Force per part = 1800 N ÷ 5 = 360 N. Force on front legs = 2 parts = 2 × 360 N = 720 N. Force on one front leg = 720 N ÷ 2 = 360 N. Area of one front leg = 15 cm² = 15 ÷ 10000 = 0.0015 m². Pressure on one front leg = 360 N ÷ 0.0015 m² = 240 000 N/m². Option C (120 000 N/m²) is a trap from using total front leg area instead of one leg. Option B (24 000 N/m²) is a trap from incorrect conversion. Option D (360 000 N/m²) is a trap from using the force value directly without proper area division.

items.question: A concrete slab exerts a pressure of 4500 N/m² on the ground when placed on one face with an area of 0.6 m². The slab is then repositioned so that its length becomes 2 times the original and its width becomes 1.5 times the original. The mass of the slab is 300 kg. What is the new pressure exerted on the ground?
items.explanation: Initial force = Pressure × Area = 4500 N/m² × 0.6 m² = 2700 N. When repositioned, new area = original area × 2 × 1.5 = 0.6 m² × 3 = 1.8 m². The force remains constant at 2700 N (same slab). New pressure = Force ÷ New Area = 2700 N ÷ 1.8 m² = 1500 N/m². The mass information is irrelevant. Option C (13 500 N/m²) is a trap from multiplying the original pressure by the area factor. Option D (9000 N/m²) is a trap from incorrect ratio application.

items.question: A metal box can rest on two different surfaces. When resting on surface A with an area of 0.25 m², it exerts a pressure of 8000 N/m². The width of surface A is 50 cm. The ratio of the area of surface A to surface B is 5:8. What pressure does the box exert when resting on surface B?
items.explanation: Force exerted by box = Pressure on A × Area of A = 8000 N/m² × 0.25 m² = 2000 N. Using ratio 5:8, if area A = 5 parts = 0.25 m², then 1 part = 0.25 ÷ 5 = 0.05 m². Area B = 8 parts = 8 × 0.05 = 0.4 m². Pressure on B = Force ÷ Area B = 2000 N ÷ 0.4 m² = 5000 N/m². The width is irrelevant. Option C (12 800 N/m²) is a trap from multiplying pressure by the ratio factor 8/5. Option D (3125 N/m²) is a trap from incorrect ratio application.

items.question: A warehouse worker places a rectangular wooden crate on the floor. The crate exerts a force of 240 N on the ground. The base of the crate measures 80 cm by 50 cm. The crate was delivered at 9:30 a.m. What is the pressure exerted by the crate on the floor in N/m²?
items.explanation: First convert dimensions to metres: length = 80 cm ÷ 100 = 0.8 m, width = 50 cm ÷ 100 = 0.5 m. Area = 0.8 m × 0.5 m = 0.4 m². Pressure = Force ÷ Area = 240 N ÷ 0.4 m² = 600 N/m². The delivery time is irrelevant information.

items.question: Two boxes, A and B, are placed on a loading platform. Together they exert a total force of 1800 N. The ratio of the force from box A to box B is 2:3. Box A has a contact area of 0.25 m² and box B has a contact area of 0.5 m². The platform is painted blue. What is the difference in pressure between box A and box B in N/m²?
items.explanation: Total ratio units = 2 + 3 = 5 units. 1 unit = 1800 N ÷ 5 = 360 N. Force from box A = 2 × 360 N = 720 N. Force from box B = 3 × 360 N = 1080 N. Pressure from box A = 720 N ÷ 0.25 m² = 2880 N/m². Pressure from box B = 1080 N ÷ 0.5 m² = 2160 N/m². Difference = 2880 N/m² - 2160 N/m² = 720 N/m². Wait, this gives 720 N/m² which is option A. Let me recalculate: Pressure A = 720 ÷ 0.25 = 2880 N/m². Pressure B = 1080 ÷ 0.5 = 2160 N/m². Difference = 2880 - 2160 = 720 N/m². The answer should be A, not B. Regenerating with corrected answer.

items.question: A hydraulic press applies a constant force of 450 N to a material. Initially, the contact area is 1.5 m². The contact area decreases at a rate of 0.2 m² per minute as the material compresses. The machine was manufactured in 2020. What is the pressure after 3 minutes of operation?
items.explanation: Area decrease = 0.2 m²/min × 3 min = 0.6 m². Final area = 1.5 m² - 0.6 m² = 0.9 m². Pressure = Force ÷ Area = 450 N ÷ 0.9 m² = 500 N/m². The manufacturing year is irrelevant. Option A (300 N/m²) is a trap from using initial pressure calculation.

items.question: A cylindrical tank with a circular base of radius 25 cm exerts a pressure of 3600 N/m² on the ground. The tank is made of stainless steel. Using π = 3.14, calculate the force exerted by the tank on the ground.
items.explanation: Convert radius to metres: 25 cm ÷ 100 = 0.25 m. Area of circular base = π × r² = 3.14 × 0.25 m × 0.25 m = 3.14 × 0.0625 m² = 0.19625 m². Force = Pressure × Area = 3600 N/m² × 0.19625 m² = 706.5 N. The tank material is irrelevant. Option A (70.65 N) is a trap from forgetting to square the radius.

items.question: An art sculpture with a mass of 180 kg stands on 4 identical legs. Each leg has a contact area of 150 cm² with the floor. items.question: A rectangular water tank has a base with length 80 cm and width 50 cm. The water inside exerts a total force of 2400 N on the base of the tank. The height of the water in the tank is 60 cm. What is the pressure exerted by the water on the base of the tank in N/cm²?
items.explanation: First, calculate the area of the base: Area = length × width = 80 cm × 50 cm = 4000 cm². Then apply the pressure formula: Pressure = Force ÷ Area = 2400 N ÷ 4000 cm² = 0.6 N/cm². Note that the height of 60 cm is given but not needed for this calculation (irrelevant datum). Option B (0.5 N/cm²) is a trap for students who might miscalculate 2400 ÷ 5000. Option C (30 N/cm²) traps students who divide force by width only (2400 ÷ 80). Option D (40 N/cm²) traps students who divide force by length only (2400 ÷ 60, incorrectly using height).
